title_en: Measures for the Administration of Military Food Supply Stations and Water Supply Stations

articles.content_en: These Measures are formulated to strengthen the administration of military catering supply stations and military water supply stations (hereinafter collectively referred to as military supply stations), and to ensure the supply of food and drinking water for the armed forces during peacetime and wartime during transportation.

Military supply stations are organizational structures and combat readiness facilities of the people's governments supporting troops in transit, and shall be managed by the veterans affairs department under the leadership of the people's governments.

The task of military supply stations is to ensure the supply of food and drinking water for troops in transit in batches, new recruits being enlisted, veterans being discharged, and militia and civilian laborers supporting the front, as well as the supply of fodder and drinking water for military transport horses.

Military supply stations shall be established by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, upon the requirements of military commands, along railways, highways, and waterways.

Military supply stations are classified into permanent stations and temporary stations. Permanent stations shall be set up at major stations on main railway and highway lines, important ports on waterways, and other places with heavy military transportation; temporary stations shall be set up at places where large-scale or emergency military transportation tasks are required, and shall be dissolved once the tasks are completed.

The basic construction items of a permanent military catering supply station shall include a kitchen, dining hall, warehouse, boiler room, office, dormitory, toilet, garage, level ground, and washing facilities, and shall, if necessary, include a horse-walking ground and horse-drinking equipment. The basic construction items of a permanent military water supply station shall include a boiler room, office, dormitory, toilet, and washing facilities.

The funds for the basic construction, facility maintenance, equipment procurement, and reception of troops in transit of military supply stations, as well as the salaries, welfare expenses, and public expenses of the permanent staff of military supply stations, shall be arranged and resolved by local finances according to the expenditure channels prescribed by the State.

A permanent military supply station shall have a small number of permanent staff, and their quota shall be determined by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government based on the military supply tasks and strategic location of the station, and shall be resolved within the total administrative establishment of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.
When encountering a large-scale military supply task and the staff of the military supply station is insufficient, the local people's government shall temporarily transfer personnel to assist the work.

When the State constructs or renovates stations and ports, the railway and transportation departments shall, in accordance with the requirements of the Military Transportation Department of the General Logistics Department, include military supply stations in the project plan and construct them together. After the completion of the project, the railway and transportation departments shall transfer the military supply stations to the veterans affairs department of the people's government. The veterans affairs department shall be responsible for the maintenance of the buildings and equipment of the military supply stations.

The military representative offices of the People's Liberation Army stationed in railway and transportation departments shall be responsible for providing operational guidance to military supply stations. When there is a large-scale military supply task, the military transportation department shall notify the military supply station in advance of the supply tasks and matters needing attention, and designate a specific person to maintain contact with the military supply station. When necessary, a military representative shall be dispatched to be stationed at the military supply station to assist in the work.

Article 11: Military supply stations shall, in accordance with relevant laws and regulations, regularly conduct security and confidentiality education for staff, and establish and improve security and confidentiality work systems.

Article 12: Military supply stations shall, in accordance with the requirements of standardized construction, achieve institutionalization, proceduralization, and standardization of work, strengthen ideological education and professional training for staff, continuously improve their adaptability and rapid support capabilities, and perform military supply work well.

Article 14: The relevant departments of the people's government at the location of the military supply station shall be responsible for the following work:
(1) The commerce, grain, supply and marketing, coal and other departments shall respectively be responsible for ensuring the supply of staple and non-staple food, fuel, necessary daily necessities, forage and feed for troops in transit, and shall provide preferential treatment in terms of variety and price in accordance with the provisions of the State and relevant departments.
(2) The health department shall be responsible for the inspection of food and water for troops in transit and the emergency treatment of the sick and wounded, and shall take in and treat those sick and wounded who cannot move with the troops. The medical expenses, meal expenses, travel expenses for returning to the unit, and funeral expenses for those who die of the sick and wounded treated in local hospitals shall be advanced by the local armed forces department and then reimbursed on a factual basis to the logistics department of the military region to which they belong.
(3) The railway and transportation departments shall be responsible for solving the power supply, communication, water supply and other equipment of military supply stations along railways, highways, and waterways.
(4) The transportation department shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions for administrative organs, reduce or exempt the road maintenance fees for motor vehicles within the authorized establishment of military supply stations.
(5) The public security department shall be responsible for public security management, traffic management, security and confidentiality work around military supply stations, and prevent possible destructive activities.

Article 15: The troops shall respect local staff, comply with the supply regulations and provisions of military supply stations, have meals based on supply notifications, and pay meal fees and grain coupons in full. When using forage and feed, they shall pay forage coupons and forage fees in full. Damage to tableware and other items shall be compensated at the original price.

Article 16: On the premise of ensuring the completion of military supply tasks, military supply stations shall combine peacetime and wartime operations, and may use existing facilities to serve the troops and to serve the society.
Article 17: These Measures shall be jointly interpreted by the Ministry of Veterans Affairs and the General Logistics Department.

Article 18: These Measures shall come into force as of the date of promulgation. The Interim Measures for the Organization and Management of Military Food Supply Stations and Water Supply Stations formulated by the General Staff Department and the Ministry of Internal Affairs, approved by the State Council on April 7, 1965, shall be abolished simultaneously.
